CHIEF COMPLAINT
Bilateral knee pain

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
62-year-old male with past medical history of kidney transplant, hypothyroidism, and arthritis presents with bilateral knee pain. Onset occurred over the weekend while moving boxes up and down basement stairs. By end of day, both knees were equally painful. Patient has had prior knee problems but attributes current symptoms to repetitive activity and weight of boxes. Tried Tylenol and ice with minimal relief. Pain was severe enough to disrupt sleep Saturday night. Denies fever, chills, muscle aches, nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies fever, chills, muscle aches, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, and headaches. Nurse performed review of systems at check-in with no additional symptoms reported.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Kidney transplant for polycystic kidney disease
Hypothyroidism
Arthritis
History of systolic ejection murmur

MEDICATIONS
Immunosuppressive medications
Synthroid

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient was moving boxes up and down basement stairs over the weekend.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: No fever, heart rate and blood pressure normal
Cardiac: 2/6 systolic ejection murmur, stable compared to prior exams
Right knee: Edema and erythema present, tenderness with palpation, decreased range of motion
Left knee: No abnormalities

RESULTS
Right knee X-ray: Good bony alignment, no acute fracture
Laboratory: White blood cell count not elevated, kidney function good

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Acute exacerbation of arthritis with right knee pain: Prescribed Ultram 50 mg every 6 hours as needed. Ordered autoimmune panel. Advised to rest. Will consider further imaging and physical therapy referral if symptoms continue over the next couple of weeks.
2. Hypothyroidism: Continue Synthroid. Ordered thyroid panel.
3. Arthritis: Monitor over next couple of weeks. Limited medication options due to kidney transplant status. Will refer to physical therapy if needed.
